changes_made.explanation: Removed baseline models that are not the main contribution of the paper. Added 'DualEnc' as the main model name. Consolidated task name to title case. Kept only the most precise output description.
The extracted metrics were already correct and properly normalized. The paper explicitly mentions using BLEU, METEOR, and TER for automatic evaluation.
No LLMs were used as judges in this 2020 paper - the paper predates the widespread use of LLMs for evaluation. The extracted metadata was already correct.

guideline: For coverage and faithfulness, workers check each triple and judge whether it's covered and faithfully described
For fluency, workers compare between two outputs of the same instance and identify which is more fluent

- For coverage and faithfulness, workers are asked to check each triple of an instance, and judge whether the triple is covered and faithfully described by the generated text. For fluency, we ask another group of workers to compare between two outputs of the same instance and identify which one is more fluent.
Annotators were asked to check each triple for coverage and faithfulness, and to compare fluency between outputs.

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated redundant guideline descriptions into two clear statements. The criteria were already correctly extracted and normalized.

overall_notes: The paper is clearly about data-to-text generation and uses both automatic metrics (BLEU, METEOR, TER) and human evaluation (coverage, faithfulness, fluency). The extraction was mostly accurate, but included too many baseline models that aren't the paper's main contribution. The paper's main model is DualEnc (also called DUALENC), which combines graph and sequential encoding.
